title: Progressive discovery and monolithic context
task_statement: Load tool and skill detail on demand, not the full catalog on every call. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Tool search tool in the Messages API
components.first_principle: Load only the tools that a request needs, found by a search tool over the full catalog.

nodes.label: Your app with the full catalog

steps: Add a tool search tool to the tools list.
Set defer_loading to true on the tools that should load later.
Keep at least one tool non-deferred, normally the search tool itself.
Claude runs a search and receives the matches as tool reference blocks.
Claude then calls a matched tool, and the API loads only the matched definitions.
pros: Tool search typically reduces tool definition tokens by over 85 percent in a multiserver setup.
Selection accuracy stays high across large catalogs, because only a focused set loads.
The MCP connector can set defer_loading once for a whole server.
cons: A tool with defer_loading true cannot carry cache_control, or the API returns 400.
On Amazon Bedrock, server-side tool search works only through the InvokeModel API, not the Converse API.
Each search adds a round trip before the tool call. (Inference)
use_when: You have 10 or more tools available.
Tool definitions use more than 10k tokens.
You aggregate several MCP servers with 200 or more tools.
do_not_use_when: You have fewer than 10 tools, or every tool is used in every request.
The tool definitions total less than 100 tokens.
A fixed workflow needs every tool visible on each turn. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Defer tool definitions to cut the tokens that each request carries.
constraints.combination: Keep the three to five most frequently used tools non-deferred.

constraints.choice: Keep the catalog focused, because each search adds a round trip.
constraints.combination: Set a higher search limit only when Claude needs more candidates. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use a catalog of up to 10,000 deferred tools for each request.
constraints.combination: Choose regex search or BM25 search for the query style that your users write.

constraints.choice: Use a service prefix in tool names, such as github_ for GitHub tools.
constraints.combination: Monitor which tools Claude discovers, and refine the descriptions that miss.

native_services.text: Server-side tool search runs only through the InvokeModel API, not the Converse API.
Server-side tool search works the same as on the Claude API.
Deployments hosted on Azure reject tool search, and the Agent SDK then loads tools upfront.

components.exam_tie: D3.8. Expect a scenario with a large tool catalog, high token cost, and wrong tool picks. The credited answer defers definitions and searches. (Inference)
components.trap: Shorter tool descriptions look cheaper. The full schemas still load on each call, so the token cost stays high. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Defer tool definitions when the catalog reaches 10 or more tools, or when definitions exceed 10k tokens.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario counts tokens per call, choose deferral over description edits. (Inference)

components.name: Agent SDK tool search
components.first_principle: The Agent SDK withholds tool definitions by default and loads matches after the agent searches.

nodes.label: Summary of tool names in context
Tool search in the agent loop

steps: The SDK withholds tool definitions from the context window.
The agent receives a summary of available tool names.
The agent searches when a task needs a tool that is not loaded.
Up to five tools that match load into context by default.
Loaded tools stay available for later turns until the SDK compacts the messages where the agent found them.
pros: Tool search is on by default in the Agent SDK.
The ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH variable sets on, off, or a threshold mode.
In auto mode, tools load upfront until their definitions reach 10 percent of the context window.
cons: Each search adds one extra round trip.
Some models on the SDK unsupported list load tools upfront, and no value overrides that.
Deployments on Microsoft Foundry hosted on Azure reject tool search.
use_when: The agent uses many MCP tools across several servers.
The context budget binds harder than round trip latency. (Inference)
You want tool search to turn on only when definitions grow. Use auto mode.
do_not_use_when: Fewer than about 10 tool definitions fit comfortably in context.
Latency binds harder than tokens, so each round trip hurts. (Inference)
The model must see every tool name before each turn. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use auto mode to load tools upfront until they reach 10 percent of the window.
constraints.combination: Use auto:5 to activate tool search at 5 percent of the window.

constraints.choice: Set ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH to false when round trips matter more than tokens.
constraints.combination: Keep the tool count low, so the agent rarely searches. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set alwaysLoad to true on a server whose tools every turn needs.
constraints.combination: Expect startup to wait for alwaysLoad servers, capped at the 5-second connect timeout.

constraints.choice: Tool search applies to remote MCP servers and custom SDK MCP servers.

native_services.text: Deployments hosted on Azure reject tool search, and the SDK loads tool definitions upfront for them.

components.exam_tie: D3.8. Expect a scenario with an SDK agent and many MCP tools. The credited answer keeps deferral on and tunes the threshold or the always-load setting. (Inference)
components.trap: A fix that turns tool search off looks simple for wrong picks. Every definition then loads on every turn, so the token cost rises.
components.decision_rule: Keep tool search on in the Agent SDK unless latency binds harder than tokens. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names a model that rejects tool search, load the tools upfront.

components.name: Agent Skills progressive disclosure
components.first_principle: Load skill metadata first, and read instructions and files only when a task needs them.

edges.label: read when the skill is relevant
read only what the task needs

steps: Put the name and description of each skill in the system prompt.
Describe the skill's purpose and the conditions that trigger it.
Claude reads SKILL.md only when the skill becomes relevant.
Claude reads reference files only as the task needs them.
Scripts run through bash, and only their output enters the context.
pros: Many skills install with little context cost, about 100 tokens each.
Reference files cost no tokens until a task reads them.
A script runs without its code in the context.
cons: A weak description can hide a useful skill from the model.
A loaded SKILL.md body costs under 5k tokens, which still competes with the conversation.
Skills on the API run with no network access and no runtime package installation.
use_when: The same domain guidance repeats across many tasks.
Reference material is large, and each task needs one part of it.
A deterministic check belongs in a script. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A one-off instruction fits in the prompt. (Inference)
The task needs live network access from the sandbox.
The guidance is short and needed on every request. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and move detail into separate files.
constraints.combination: Use scripts for checks, so only their output costs tokens.

constraints.choice: Use a name of up to 64 characters with lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
constraints.combination: Use a description of up to 1,024 characters that says when to use the skill.

constraints.choice: Split content by domain, so one task reads one file.
Custom Skills on the Claude API are shared across the whole workspace.
constraints.combination: Use a separate workspace for a tenant whose Skills must stay private. (Inference)

native_services.text: Skills follow the same behavior as the Claude API. Upload custom Skills through the Skills API.
Skills follow the same behavior as the Claude API. Pre-built Agent Skills require a Hosted on Anthropic deployment. The Skill version download endpoint is not supported.

components.exam_tie: D3.8. Expect a scenario with a large body of guidance and a token budget. The credited answer loads the smallest needed part on demand. (Inference)
components.trap: A system prompt that holds every reference file looks thorough. Each token then competes with the conversation for context space.
components.decision_rule: Put only metadata in the prompt, and load each file when the task needs it.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names large reference documents, choose skill files over a longer system prompt. (Inference)

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Tool or guidance catalog large?} -->|No| B[Load everything upfront]
  A -->|Yes| C{Latency binds harder than tokens?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Keep core tools loaded upfront]
  C -->|No| E{Tools or guidance?}
  E -->|Tools| F[Tool search with defer_loading true]
  E -->|Guidance| G[Skills with progressive disclosure]
  F --> H[Keep three to five frequent tools non-deferred]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  M[Metadata first] --> S[Search or select]
  S --> T[Tool search tool]
  S --> K[Skills files]
  T --> L[Load up to 5 matches]
  K --> R[Read only needed files]
  L --> C[Lower tokens per call]
  R --> C

patterns.rule: Show fewer tools per turn, and load matches on demand.
traps: Larger model that reads all schemas

patterns.rule: Keep metadata in the prompt, and read files on demand.
